family.description: The Tail Tip Fiber Protein family includes proteins involved in the attachment and penetration of bacteriophages into host cells. Members of this family are responsible for recognizing and irreversibly binding to specific host receptors, which triggers structural changes in the viral tail necessary for the injection of viral DNA into the host. This process is critical for the successful infection and propagation of the virus. The family includes proteins that initiate distal tail tip assembly during phage tail assembly and play a key role in the virus entry by mediating the attachment to the host receptor and inducing DNA ejection through the receptor's pore. This entry represents the beta prism domain which is formed from a homotrimeric complex of members of this family.
family.name: Bacteriophage tail tip fiber protein
